summary: Hand-written regex detectors screen surface properties; 8 align perfectly with the label in every sample. The gradient proxy F@g is calibrated against SAE logits, then regressed on the 8 properties over the corpus and, more cleanly, over a 64-note-per-probe synthetic factorial (topic x 8 properties) built by a programmatic note generator. Dependence = property coefficient / topic coefficient, with 0.15/0.3 bands. Ambiguous or borderline candidates are measured with true logits on single-property toggles from an all-off baseline and compared to the proxy on the same texts. Ablation latents are ranked by per-latent regression coefficient x gradient with topic-drain filters, inspected via latent_examples, verified by sample ablation and corpus mean-ablation, and diffuse cues re-selected from corpus-derived contributions.

phases.purpose: Read task file, sample notes and corpus to see how notes are decorated
Regex detectors for 12 surface properties; per-probe label alignment identifies 8 perfectly aligned candidates
Pilot on probe 0: fit SAE logit against F@g on sample notes to validate the gradient proxy
Encode the corpus in 64-text batches; collect gradients, scores and sample activations for probes 1-3
Corpus OLS of F@g on 8 properties; topic effect from sample gap minus signed property effects; dependence ratios with standard errors
Programmatic note generator; random factorial of 64 notes per probe varying topic and all 8 properties; OLS dependences
True logits on single toggles for ambiguous/borderline candidates (probe 0 excl and bullet, probe 3 greeting); proxy on same texts to estimate per-property compression; decide cue sets
Per-latent contributions (per-latent design coefficient x gradient); per-cue then joint greedy selection under a 20% topic-drain cap
Inspect top tokens of the strongest candidate latents to confirm they encode the property rather than topic
Capture ceiling for diffuse cues; selection with per-latent topic filter (strict 0.06 dropped, tuned 0.13)
Ablate chosen latents on sample notes; check topic gap and separation accuracy
Corpus balanced accuracy of cue regexes; reassemble selection with 0.15 per-latent topic filter and pronoun 3 / closing-question 13 split; build answer
Corpus cross-validation by mean-ablating columns; re-select hashtag and closing-question latents from corpus-derived contributions

probe_query_use.purpose: Measure true exclamation dependence relative to the topic flip, which the proxy put in the ambiguous band

probe_query_use.text_kind: all-off note for each topic plus first-topic note with a greeting line added
probe_query_use.purpose: Check whether the strongest candidate on a probe that looked cue-free crosses the cue threshold

probe_query_use.text_kind: all-off first-topic note with bullet formatting switched on
probe_query_use.purpose: Check the second-largest candidate on probe 0

per_probe.conclusion: exclamation-mark punctuation (sentences end with ! instead of .)
per_probe.procedure: Corpus regression and the factorial both put exclamation as the largest dependence but in the ambiguous 0.15-0.3 band (factorial 0.25). A true-logit single toggle gave about 0.4-0.47, so it was declared a cue. Bullet formatting also toggled large on true logits but was rejected because its proxy toggle effect greatly exceeded its factorial main effect, read as an interaction off the all-off baseline. Regex '!' over the whole note. Sixteen latents chosen from the factorial per-latent contribution ranking (same sign as the cue, per-latent topic contribution <=0.15), deliberately overshooting proxy removal to offset the error term; latent 9330 was seen firing on '!' tokens.
per_probe.quote: excl IS a main cue (F@g underestimated it at 0.25)

per_probe.procedure: Factorial dependence for hashtag 0.331 sat above a clear break from the next property (0.155), consistent with the corpus regression. Regex '#\w'. Latents first ranked by factorial contribution with a topic filter, inspected (13688 on '#', 6769/9158 on hashtag word pieces), then re-selected from corpus-derived per-latent coefficients x gradient (threshold 0.005, factorial topic contribution <=0.15) because the generator's hashtag words differed from the corpus; corpus mean-ablation removal improved slightly. Sixteen latents.

per_probe.conclusion: two cues: female pronoun (she/her) and closing phrased as 'would you try it with...?'
per_probe.procedure: Factorial dependences 0.97 for pronoun and 0.42 for the closing question, both far above the rest. Regexes: case-insensitive she/her/hers word match, and 'would you try'. Pronoun effect concentrated in three latents (15104, 3344, 5115); a strict per-latent topic filter wrongly dropped two of them, so the filter was loosened. Closing-question effect is diffuse; 13 latents re-selected from corpus-derived contributions excluding the pronoun latents. Union of 16 latents; sample ablation kept perfect topic separation.

Factorial dependences were all at or below 0.145 with no break in the sorted list. The top candidate, greeting line, was measured with true logits on a single toggle, giving roughly 0.21 against the topic flip, and its true/proxy ratio was near 1, so the factorial value stood below the cue threshold. Answered none.

decision_points.choice: Twelve regex property detectors written after reading sample notes; those perfectly aligned with label in every probe (8) became candidates
decision_points.quote: The confound set is clear: **8 properties** perfectly separate the label in every probe (polarity flips per probe)

decision_points.choice: Programmatic note generator; random factorial of 64 notes per probe over topic and 8 properties; hand-picked single toggles from an all-off baseline for true logits
decision_points.quote: Let me build a **controlled synthetic factorial** (topic × 8 props varied independently) to measure all coefficients directly and cleanly

decision_points.choice: Gradient proxy F@g validated against SAE logits, regressed on property design (corpus, then factorial); dependence = property coef / topic coef
decision_points.quote: Calibration is strong: `corr(F@g, true_logit)=0.976`, clean linear fit.

decision_points.choice: 4 texts on probe 0 exclamation, then 3 on probe 3 greeting and 1 on probe 0 bullet
decision_points.quote: Let me resolve the remaining borderlines with my last 4 probe_query texts: P3 (is it really none? — measure its top candidate `greeting` + topic baseline) and P0's top competitor `bullet`.

decision_points.choice: None when sorted factorial dependences show no break and the top candidate stays under 0.3 after true-logit check
decision_points.quote: Sorted factorial F@g dependences show a clear break after each probe's cue(s)

decision_points.choice: Factorial varies all candidates independently; single-toggle true effects normalized by topic flip; large toggle rejected when proxy toggle far exceeds factorial main effect
decision_points.quote: The P0 bullet single-toggle (0.42) was interaction-inflated off the extreme all-off baseline (its single-toggle F@g 0.273 ≫ factorial main-effect 0.157).

decision_points.choice: Minimal pattern per cue, all scope any, checked by balanced accuracy against the detector on the corpus
decision_points.quote: All regexes hit **balanced accuracy 1.000** on the corpus.

decision_points.choice: Per-latent design coefficient x gradient, same sign as cue, greedy by magnitude with topic-drain cap / per-latent topic filter; budget split 3/13 for the two-cue probe
decision_points.quote: Since mean-ablation removes each latent's contribution analytically (constant columns drop from regression slopes), I can select optimal sets directly.

decision_points.choice: latent_examples token inspection, probe_scores ablation on sample (gap and separation accuracy), corpus mean-ablation removal
decision_points.quote: **topic separation stays perfect** (sepAcc 1.00) for all three

decision_points.choice: Three probes with cues (1,1,2 cues), 16 latents each; one none
Diffuse-cue latents re-selected from corpus-derived contributions instead of the synthetic factorial
decision_points.quote: Let me re-select those latents using **corpus-derived** contributions (the real generator distribution) for better generalization.

caveats: Several outputs were truncated (corpus regression table for probes 2-3, factorial rows for probes 2-3, latent ranking for later cues), so exact intermediate values are partly inferred. The cue decision combined a threshold rule with a judgment about interaction inflation; the script encodes the final sets as an inspection constant. The compression-correction rule is reconstructed from the session's narrative rather than an explicit code step. Several selection variants were run with small parameter changes; their exact ordering and which output fed the final latents (factorial for exclamation and pronoun, corpus for hashtag and closing question) are taken from the final assembly step.
